note: The most famous Chinese number code. Said quickly, wǔ-èr-líng sounds close to wǒ-ài-nǐ, so typing 520 became a shy, playful way to say “I love you” online. It also gave May 20 its status as an internet-born love day, when couples exchange gifts, send red packets of 5.20 or 520 yuan and register marriages.
use: Texts, comments, red-packet amounts, gift tags, May 20 promotions, wedding-registration dates.
label: Love code

note: The companion to 520. Read as “I’m willing” (as in “I do”) or simply another “I love you”, it makes May 21 a popular date for proposals and the reply to a 520 message.
use: Replies to 520, proposal dates, couples’ anniversaries.
label: Love code

note: Yī-sān-yī-sì echoes yī-shēng-yī-shì — “one life, one world”, i.e. forever. Here the 4 borrows the sound shì (world) instead of its unlucky reading, which is why 1314 is one of the few loved numbers that contains a 4.
use: Red packets of 13.14 or 1314, wedding dates, jewellery engravings, combined as 5201314.
label: Love code

py: wǒ ài nǐ yī shēng yī shì
m: I love you for a lifetime
note: 520 plus 1314: the long-form love vow. It is one of the most searched and most gifted number messages, used in captions, bracelets, flower orders and anniversary cards.
use: Anniversary messages, engagement captions, couple accessories.
label: Love code

py: yī shēng yī shì wǒ ài nǐ
m: for a lifetime, I love you
note: The reverse order of 5201314 — same promise, different emphasis, often used as a reply to it.
use: Replies, couple usernames, phone-number wish lists.
label: Love code

note: Here 3 stands in for xiǎng (to miss / think of). A gentle long-distance code that pairs naturally with 520.
label: Love code

note: A confession code: 5-2-3-0 ≈ wǒ ài shàng nǐ. Typically used early in a relationship, before the more committed 1314.
label: Love code

note: 9 here is jiù (“just / only”). Short, sweet and exclusive.

note: Jiù-shì-ài-nǐ: “it’s simply you I love.” Another code where 4 reads as shì (is), not as the unlucky sǐ.

note: Read as yī-jiù-ài-nǐ, “still loving you” — popular for long marriages and reconciliations.

note: Yī-qī-yī-yī ≈ yī-xīn-yī-yì: with one heart and one mind. Used for devotion to a partner and, in business, to customers.

note: Bā-líng-yī-sān ≈ bàn-nǐ-yī-shēng — “accompany you all my life.”

note: Triple nine intensifies longevity — eternal love, lasting health, a business that endures.

note: A blessing for relationships and partnerships: may it last long.

note: 5 (wǒ) + 1 (yào) + 8 (fā). Loved by entrepreneurs; May 18 is a popular business-launch date.

note: The best-known money number in Chinese culture. Phone numbers, plates and prices with 888 often carry a premium.

note: Four eights: the 4 count is outweighed by the sheer number of “fā”. A luxury signal on plates and phone numbers.

note: Our composite reading of this site’s name: 520 (“I love you”) joined to 998 (“long-lasting prosperity”). Its digits sum to 33, a so-called master number in Western numerology. It is a blessing for love that lasts and a life that prospers.
use: This site’s motto; wedding and anniversary wishes; launch-day greetings for couple-run businesses.
